newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish police intervenes against union protests.
newsitem.headline: Polish police intervenes against union protests.

text.p: Polish riot police on Wednesday surrounded and entered two ministries occupied by Solidarity members protesting against closure of the Gdansk shipyard, and the union's chiefs threatened to react sharply to any use of force.

"What is happening in Warsaw is clearly a provocation," Solidarity leader Marian Krzaklewski told a news conference, adding that the union leadership would hold a crisis meeting later in the afternoon to agree on a response to the police action.

The union launched a nation-wide protest on Wednesday, demonstrating in the northern port city of Gdansk and occupying the Warsaw ministries of the Treasury, Finance and Economy, to demand government action to save the bankrupt shipyard.
Outside the Treasury ministry, Solidarity spokesman Piotr Zak told Reuters the police had issued an ultimatum and tried to push workers out of the building, but had failed.
Police spokesman Witold Gieralt confirmed to Reuters that the police had entered the ministry buildings and at the Treasury another spokesman said they had orders to avoid violence.

Solidarity leaders told the news conference union reinforcements were converging on Warsaw and Krzaklewski said the union's charter allowed it to call a general strike if force was used against it, although it would adopt other, unspecified measures first.
